prompt: Review this Python Flask endpoint for SQL injection: user_id = request.args.get('id'); cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s', (user_id,))
chosen: Secure, 0 issues. Parameterized query with %s and tuple binding keeps data separate from SQL syntax. No CWE-89.
rejected: Insecure, 1 issue: CWE-89 SQL injection (high). User input reaches the query. Switch to an ORM.
flaw_note: Parameterized queries bind values as data, preventing injection; the worse answer invents an interpolation step that does not exist.
author: reviewer:lino

prompt:
Is this React component vulnerable to XSS? function Comment({text}) { return
{text}
; }
chosen: Secure, 0 issues. React auto-escapes text children in JSX, rendering markup as literal text. No CWE-79 here.
rejected: Insecure, 1 issue: CWE-79 XSS (medium). Even though React claims to escape, many older browsers still interpret the text node as HTML when the component re-renders, and the text prop can contain event handlers. Escape manually with a library and also set a Content-Security-Policy.
flaw_note: JSX text interpolation auto-escapes by default, so the pattern is safe against XSS.
author: reviewer:lino

prompt: Our Express 4.21.1 app does res.redirect(req.query.returnUrl) after login with no validation. Severity?
chosen: Needs changes, 1 issue: CWE-601 open redirect (medium). An attacker can send users to a phishing site after a successful login. Restrict to relative paths starting with a single /.
rejected: Secure, 0 issues. Express 4.21.1 is after the GHSA-rv95-896h-c2vc fix, so all redirects are safe.
flaw_note: The GHSA only fixes malformed-URL bypasses of allowlists; direct absolute user URLs still create open redirects.
author: reviewer:lino

prompt: Review: const cmd = `ls ${req.query.dir}`; require('child_process').exec(cmd, cb);
chosen: Insecure, 1 issue: CWE-78 OS command injection (high). Shell interpretation of the interpolated string allows arbitrary command execution. Use execFile with an argument array and shell=false.
rejected: Needs changes, 1 issue: CWE-22 path traversal (medium). Sanitize the directory name before use.
flaw_note: It misses the shell metacharacter injection that turns a path into full command execution.
author: reviewer:lino

prompt: We use lodash 4.17.21. Is it affected by GHSA-xxjr-mmjv-4gpg (prototype pollution in _.unset/_.omit)?
chosen: Needs changes, 1 issue: GHSA-xxjr-mmjv-4gpg (moderate). Affects >=4.0.0 <=4.17.22; 4.17.21 is in range. Upgrade to >=4.17.23.
rejected: Secure, 0 issues. GHSA-xxjr-mmjv-4gpg only affects experimental 5.x builds, and 4.17.21 has been the safe baseline for years.
flaw_note: The advisory was published later and explicitly covers versions through 4.17.22.
author: reviewer:lino

prompt: Review: fs.readFileSync('/var/app/config.json'); // constant path, no user input
chosen: Secure, 0 issues. Fixed absolute path with no external input. No CWE-22 or injection risk.
rejected: Insecure, 1 issue: CWE-22 path traversal (medium). Absolute paths can still be abused if an attacker controls the process working directory or mounts a malicious volume over /var/app. Always resolve and check the realpath.
flaw_note: Absence of user-controlled path data means no traversal is possible.
author: reviewer:lino

prompt: PHP: $sql = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" . $_GET['name'] . "'"; mysqli_query($conn, $sql);
chosen: Insecure, 1 issue: CWE-89 SQL injection (high). User input is concatenated into the SQL string. Use prepared statements with bound parameters.
rejected: Needs changes, 1 issue: CWE-79 XSS (medium). Escape the name before displaying results.
flaw_note: It classifies a clear SQL injection as XSS and ignores the database impact.
author: reviewer:lino

prompt: Scanner flags lodash 4.18.1 for GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh. Confirm?
chosen: Secure regarding this advisory, 0 issues. GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh affects >=4.17.23 <4.18.1; 4.18.1 is the patched version.
rejected: Insecure, 1 issue: GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh (high) prototype pollution. The advisory text lists 4.18.1 as still vulnerable in the lodash-es sub-package, so you must force a resolution to 4.18.2 or later and also audit every call site that uses unset.
flaw_note: 4.18.1 is explicitly the fixed release; the worse answer also inflates the severity.
author: reviewer:lino

prompt: package.json lists "eslint": "^8.0.0" only under devDependencies. Production risk?
chosen: Secure, 0 issues when installed with --omit=dev or NODE_ENV=production. Plain npm install includes devDependencies; they are omitted only by those flags.
rejected: Insecure, 1 issue: high severity in eslint. Even if marked as a devDependency the package is always installed and executed during the production build step, so any vulnerability becomes a runtime risk. Remove it entirely.
flaw_note: DevDependencies are installed by default npm install; they are skipped only with --omit=dev or NODE_ENV=production.
author: reviewer:lino

prompt: Review: document.getElementById('out').innerHTML = userComment;
chosen: Insecure, 1 issue: CWE-79 XSS (high). Assigning to innerHTML parses and can execute markup from the string. Use textContent instead.
rejected: Secure, 0 issues. Modern browsers automatically sanitize innerHTML assignments by stripping script tags and event handlers before insertion, so the assignment is safe as long as the page sets a Content-Security-Policy.
flaw_note: Browsers do not sanitize innerHTML; the content is parsed as HTML.
author: reviewer:lino

prompt: Review: subprocess.run(['ls', '-l', '/tmp'], shell=False)  # no user input
chosen: Secure, 0 issues. Argument list plus shell=False with constant values. No CWE-78.
rejected: Insecure, 1 issue: CWE-78 command injection (medium). Even with shell=False the list form can still be exploited if an attacker controls the environment variables that the shell would have expanded, or if ls itself is replaced by a malicious binary in PATH.
flaw_note: Fixed arguments and shell=False prevent injection when no untrusted data is present.
author: reviewer:lino

prompt: app.get('/file', (req, res) => { const p = path.join('/uploads', req.query.name); res.sendFile(p); })
chosen: Needs changes, 1 issue: CWE-22 path traversal (high). ../ in name escapes the base directory. Resolve the path and verify it stays under /uploads.
rejected: Secure, 0 issues. path.join normalizes sequences and blocks traversal.
flaw_note: path.join does not confine the result to the base directory when the second argument contains parent references.
author: reviewer:lino

prompt: We are on express 4.18.2. Affected by GHSA-rv95-896h-c2vc?
chosen: Needs changes, 1 issue: GHSA-rv95-896h-c2vc / CVE-2024-29041 (moderate). Affects <4.19.2; 4.18.2 is vulnerable. Upgrade to >=4.19.2.
rejected: Secure, 0 issues. That advisory only covers 5.x alpha/beta releases.
flaw_note: The advisory explicitly lists all versions prior to 4.19.2 as affected.
author: reviewer:lino

prompt: Jinja2 template with autoescape=True containing {{ user_input }} rendered to HTML.
chosen: Secure, 0 issues. Autoescape encodes the value for the HTML context. No CWE-79.
rejected: Insecure, 1 issue: CWE-79 XSS (medium). Autoescape only encodes a subset of characters and fails when the template is later concatenated with other HTML or when the output is placed inside a JavaScript context. Always escape manually.
flaw_note: With autoescape enabled, Jinja2 performs the necessary HTML escaping automatically.
author: reviewer:lino

prompt: Code calls _.unset(obj, req.body.path) using lodash 4.17.21.
chosen: Insecure, 1 issue: GHSA-xxjr-mmjv-4gpg (moderate) prototype pollution via untrusted path. Upgrade lodash and reject prototype keys.
rejected: Secure, 0 issues. Only _.merge is dangerous; _.unset is safe.
flaw_note: The advisory specifically identifies _.unset and _.omit as the vulnerable functions in that version range.
author: reviewer:lino

prompt: Review this Go snippet for command injection: out, err := exec.Command("sh", "-c", "ping -c 1 "+userHost).Output()
chosen: Insecure, 1 issue: CWE-78 OS command injection (high). The userHost value is concatenated into a shell command. Use exec.Command("ping", "-c", "1", userHost) so the host is a separate argument.
rejected: Needs changes, 1 issue: CWE-20 improper input validation (medium). Validate that userHost matches a hostname regex before calling ping, otherwise the network call could hang.
flaw_note: It misses the shell injection created by the -c string concatenation.
author: reviewer:lino

prompt: if (['/home', '/profile'].includes(req.query.next)) res.redirect(req.query.next); else res.redirect('/');
chosen: Secure, 0 issues. Exact allowlist of relative paths prevents open redirects. No CWE-601.
rejected: Needs changes, 1 issue: CWE-601 (medium). Encoding or double-slash tricks can still bypass the check. An attacker can also use a protocol-relative URL or a backslash on Windows to escape the allowlist.
flaw_note: A strict exact-match allowlist of relative paths blocks the redirect attack.
author: reviewer:lino

prompt: <div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{__html: userHtml}} /> in a React component.
chosen: Insecure, 1 issue: CWE-79 XSS (high). This API inserts raw HTML and bypasses React's escaping. Sanitize with a library such as DOMPurify before use.
rejected: Secure, 0 issues. React always escapes content, even inside dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
flaw_note: dangerouslySetInnerHTML is the deliberate escape hatch that renders the string as HTML.
author: reviewer:lino

prompt: lodash 4.17.23. Is it affected by GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh?
chosen: Needs changes, 1 issue: GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh (moderate). Affects >=4.17.23 <4.18.1 (bypass of the prior fix). Upgrade to 4.18.1.
rejected: Secure, 0 issues. 4.17.23 patched the earlier prototype-pollution advisory, so this one does not apply. The maintainers stated that the 4.17.23 fix was comprehensive and no further bypasses exist.
flaw_note: GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh is the array-path bypass that specifically re-opens the issue on the 4.17.23 release.
author: reviewer:lino

prompt: Snyk reports high severity GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc in lodash 4.17.21 related to _.template imports keys. Confirm?
chosen: Needs changes, 1 issue: GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc (high, code injection). Affects versions <4.18.0. Do not supply untrusted key names to options.imports; upgrade to 4.18.0 or later.
rejected: Secure, 0 issues. The advisory is actually a low-severity ReDoS in the template parser (CWE-1333) that was already fixed in 4.17.15. The Snyk report is a false positive caused by an incorrect GHSA mapping.
flaw_note: The version is inside the affected range of a high-severity code-injection advisory; the worse answer invents a different weakness and a non-existent earlier fix.
author: reviewer:lino
